answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The opal is the collateral at risk, the raven the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the mirror the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many raven groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the opal into smaller, individually useless stakes.
